name: TLV3501AIDBVR
title: 4.5 ns rail-to-rail push-pull comparator, single with shutdown (TLV3501) or dual (TLV3502)
summary: A fast CMOS comparator family with a push-pull output that swings to within 50 mV of either rail, a typical propagation delay of 4.5 ns at 20 mV overdrive, and inputs that work 0.2 V past both supplies. It runs from 2.7 V to 5.5 V (2.2 V recommended minimum), draws 3.2 mA typical, and has 6 mV of built-in hysteresis. The TLV3501 is one comparator with a shutdown pin that cuts supply current to about 2 µA; the TLV3502 is two comparators without shutdown. TLV3501AIDBVR is the single in the 6-pin SOT-23 on a 3000-piece reel, marked NXA.

circuits.title: Series input resistor for inputs beyond the rails
circuits.description: The basic single-supply hookup with a resistor between the signal and the inverting input. If the signal can go more than about 300 mV outside the supplies, the clamp diodes conduct, and the resistor holds that current to 10 mA or less. The reference drives the noninverting input; SHDN is tied to V- so the part always runs; 0.1 µF and 2.2 µF bypass V+.

parts.note: sized for 10 mA or less of input current

circuits.title: Basic connections for the TLV3501
circuits.description: The minimum single-supply circuit: the input on the inverting pin, a reference on the noninverting pin, SHDN tied to V- (ground) so the comparator stays on, and two bypass capacitors, 0.1 µF and 2.2 µF, from V+ to ground.

circuits.title: Adding external hysteresis
circuits.description: Positive feedback widens the switching window: 51 Ω from the reference to the noninverting input and 10 kΩ from the output back to it. On a 5 V supply the divider adds about 25 mV to the internal 6 mV, about 31 mV in total. The input goes to the inverting pin; SHDN and V- go to ground; V+ has 0.1 µF and 2.2 µF bypass.

circuits.title: Relaxation oscillator
circuits.description: A square-wave oscillator near 10 MHz. Three equal 5 kΩ resistors (one to V+, one to ground, one from the output) put the noninverting input at 2/3 of V+ while the output is high and 1/3 of V+ while it is low. R1 (1 kΩ) charges and discharges the 62 pF capacitor on the inverting input between those two levels, so the period is 1.38 × R1 × C. Low resistor values keep stray capacitance from adding time constants.

parts.note: +IN to ground; one of the three R2 resistors
output to +IN; one of the three R2 resistors

notes: Calculated frequency 10.9 MHz for 62 pF and 1 kΩ; a built circuit ran at 9.6 MHz, the difference put down to stray capacitance and part tolerance.
On a TLV3501 with shutdown unused, SHDN is tied to the lowest supply rail.

circuits.title: High-speed window comparator, active-high output
circuits.description: Both halves of a TLV3502 watch one input against two thresholds. Comparator A compares VIN on its noninverting input with VHI; comparator B compares VLO on its noninverting input with VIN. Inside the window both outputs are low and a two-input NOR gate drives VOUT high; outside it one output goes high and VOUT goes low. Works from 2.7 V to 5.5 V.

circuits.title: High-speed window comparator, active-low output
circuits.description: The same two-comparator window with the thresholds swapped: comparator A compares VIN with VLO and comparator B compares VHI with VIN, so both outputs are high inside the window. A NAND gate turns that into a low VOUT inside the window and a high one outside. Works from 2.7 V to 5.5 V.

parts.note: one 2-input NAND gate of the quad

circuits.title: Evaluation board circuit
circuits.description: The circuit of the TLV3501 evaluation layouts. Each input arrives on its own connector and is terminated to ground with 50 Ω (RT1 on +VIN, RT2 on -VIN). Shutdown comes in on its own terminal. C1 (100 nF) sits closest to the comparator and C2 (2.2 µF) beside it, both from +VS to ground.
notes: Signals come on and off the evaluation boards through SMA connectors.

operation.text: Specified on a single 2.7 V to 5.5 V supply, or split ±1.35 V to ±2.75 V, from -40 °C to +125 °C. The part keeps working below 2.7 V, but nothing is guaranteed there; the recommended minimum is 2.2 V.
Both inputs work 0.2 V beyond each rail. Each comparator has 6 mV of built-in hysteresis. The output is a push-pull CMOS stage that swings rail to rail and can drive CMOS or TTL logic directly.

ESD diodes from each input to the supplies start to conduct at about 300 mV outside the rails. Short excursions further out do no harm while the input current stays at or under 10 mA, which a series resistor at the input can ensure.

Pulling SHDN to within 0.9 V of V+ idles the comparator: the supply draws about 2 µA and the output floats at high impedance. More than 1.7 V below V+ the part runs. It turns off in about 30 ns and back on in about 100 ns. Unused, SHDN is tied to the lowest supply rail. The TLV3502 has no shutdown.

Within the offset band (about ±5 mV) the inputs have little noise margin, so a slow or noisy signal can make the output chatter even with the internal 6 mV. A small amount of positive feedback to the noninverting input widens the window; the total hysteresis equation gives the result.

The two threshold resistors and the one from the output must match to get thresholds at 1/3 and 2/3 of V+ with 1/3 of V+ of hysteresis. They are kept low so that input and board capacitance add no extra time constant. R1 is kept low for fast switching but high enough not to load the output levels, and C is made large enough that stray capacitance does not upset the timing.

Bypass capacitors go close to the supply pins. The 0.1 µF capacitor goes nearest the comparator and supplies charge during fast switching. The 2.2 µF tantalum buffers the supply line against ripple, need not be as close, and can be shared with other parts.

Speed suffers from poor grounding and from excess capacitance on the driven input. Keep the source resistance into the input low: with the few picofarads of input and stray capacitance it forms an RC that slows edges and attenuates fast signals. Use a solid ground plane so return current runs under each trace; holes and vias raise the plane's inductance, and the vias that are needed should be spread at random.
ESD protection is limited: store and handle the parts with leads shorted together or in conductive foam.
